name: cdrdao
why: Disk-at-once CD recording exposes the raw optical track layout and needs a real burner, a physical hands-on curiosity.

brief.what_it_is: Cdrdao is a command-line tool for burning audio or data CD-Rs and CD-RWs in disk-at-once (DAO) mode, driven by a plain-text description of the disc contents called a toc-file. The toc-file specifies the tracks, pre-gaps, and sub-channel data, and cdrdao writes the whole disc (lead-in, tracks, lead-out) in one pass. The homepage describes accepting WAVE and raw audio files as input. It also supports reading and writing CD-TEXT on drives that support it, copying audio, data, and mixed-mode discs, and creating CD-TEXT from CDDB lookups. The executables listed in the brief (cdrdao, cue2toc, toc2cddb, toc2cue, toc2mp3) are not named on the homepage, so I did not confirm what the helper tools do.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage argues that track-at-once recording cannot define the data written in pre-gaps, which makes features like hidden bonus tracks or track intros impossible, while disk-at-once recording gives full control of the disc. It also says DAO is the only way to write to the R-W sub-channels needed for CD-G or CD-TEXT.
brief.how_it_works: A toc-file describes the disc contents, and cdrdao writes the complete disc in a single step, including lead-in and lead-out, so pre-gaps can be omitted, filled, or lengthened. Sub-channel fields such as catalog number, ISRC, index marks, and copy/pre-emphasis flags are set from the description. The homepage does not explain the implementation beyond this.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install appears on the homepage. Using it requires a CD recorder drive; the homepage links to Supported Drives and Available Drivers pages, which I did not fetch. The scout note's point that a real burner is needed is consistent with the homepage's focus on writing physical discs, but the homepage itself does not spell out hardware requirements.
brief.standout: Its approach gives direct, fine-grained control over the physical disc layout, including pre-gap contents and sub-channel data, where most burning tools hide that layout. It treats the disc as a textual, editable description rather than a list of files.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage shows no release date, version number, or last-updated note, and I did not reach the Download or Changelog pages to check.
brief.caveats: The homepage lists platforms that have 'reported to work' (FreeBSD, IRIX, Linux, Solaris, HP-UX, Win32, OS/2, UnixWare), which is weaker than a support guarantee. Writing to a disc is irreversible for CD-R media. The homepage does not state a license. The executables list in the brief may not match what the homepage describes, and I did not verify it.
quotes: Cdrdao records audio or data CD-Rs in disk-at-once (DAO) mode based on a textual description of the CD contents (toc-file).
Recording in disk-at-once mode writes the complete disc, i.e. lead-in, one or more tracks and lead-out, in a single step.
DAO recording is the only way to write data to the unused R-W sub-channels for e.g. CD-G or CD-TEXT.
fetch_log: https://cdrdao.sourceforge.net/ : fetched successfully. It is a plain HTML page, not a GitHub README. It has navigation links to Application Examples, Available Drivers, Supported Drives, Download, and Changelog, but the page text gives no URLs for them, so I did not follow them.
